name: Question 1
problem: Given that ${i,j,k}$ is the standard basis of ${R}^{3}$ and that the images of $i,$ $j,$ and $k$ under the action of a linear transformation $T$ are $⟨6,2,0⟩,$ $⟨-3,5,6⟩,$ and $⟨-1,2,7⟩,$ respectively, what is the standard matrix of $T?$
worked_solution:
Every linear transformation in ${R}^{3}$ can be represented as a $3\times 3$ matrix. The standard matrix representation of the transformation has columns that are the images of the vectors $i,j,$ and $k$ under the action of the transformation.

Therefore, the standard matrix for the linear transformation is 

$$
T=[\begin{aligned}6 & -3 & -1 \\ 2 & 5 & 2 \\ 0 & 6 & 7\end{aligned}].
$$

Question 1
?

Given that {i,j,k} is the standard basis of R3 and that the images of i, j, and k under the action of a linear transformation T are ⟨6,2,0⟩, ⟨−3,5,6⟩, and ⟨−1,2,7⟩, respectively, what is the standard matrix of T?

a
[6−3−1252067]
b
[−127−356620]
c
[0672526−3−1]
d
[0676−3−1252]
e
[620−356−127]
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

Every linear transformation in R3 can be represented as a 3×3 matrix. The standard matrix representation of the transformation has columns that are the images of the vectors i,j, and k under the action of the transformation.

Therefore, the standard matrix for the linear transformation is T=[6−3−1252067].
